How BelivrHQ and PappyCoder Technologies Limited collect, use, disclose, retain and protect personal information, and how to exercise your privacy rights.
PappyCoder Technologies Limited · Nigeria
On this page

BelivrHQ is operated by PappyCoder Technologies Limited, a company based in Nigeria ("BelivrHQ", "we", "us" or "our"). This Privacy Policy explains our handling of personal information through our website, account services, church management platform, support channels and connected features. It also explains the different responsibilities of BelivrHQ and the churches that use the platform.

This Policy is a notice about data processing. Reading it, visiting the website or accepting our commercial terms does not, by itself, provide consent for every use of personal information. Where consent is required, it must be obtained for the relevant purpose. Mandatory privacy rights remain available regardless of any contractual limitation.
Important points to read first
These points help you navigate the document. Read the full provisions that follow.
1. Scope and application

This Policy applies to website visitors, account holders, church administrators and staff, people who contact us, and people whose information is entered into a BelivrHQ workspace. It covers information collected directly, supplied by a church or another authorised person, generated through use of the service, or received from a connected provider.

A church may operate its own website, publish a form, organise an event, collect giving or communicate through a provider connected to BelivrHQ. That church must provide its own privacy information for its activities. Our Policy does not replace the church’s notices or the notices of payment processors, communications providers, video platforms and other independent services.

The Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 and applicable implementing instruments inform this Policy. Other mandatory privacy laws may also apply depending on the people, organisations and processing concerned. We do not represent that the platform is automatically suitable for every country, sector or regulated use.
2. Who is responsible for your information

For information processed to run our business (such as account contact details, subscription payments, enquiries, platform security and our own legal compliance), PappyCoder Technologies Limited generally acts as a data controller, determining the relevant purposes and means of processing.

For information a church submits or generates in its workspace, the church generally acts as controller and BelivrHQ acts as processor on the church’s documented instructions. An authorised administrator’s use of the platform and agreed settings form part of those instructions. The precise legal role depends on the actual activity, not only the label used in this Policy.

A church’s administrators manage access to its workspace, including branch assignments, roles, permissions, invitations, exports and public sharing. Staff, volunteers or contractors with access act under that church’s authority. BelivrHQ support cannot automatically override a church’s permissions or disclose its records merely because a person asks for them.

If your request concerns a church record, contact the church first where practical. You may also contact us directly. We will identify our role, verify the request as appropriate and assist or refer it to the responsible church without preventing you from exercising rights against us where we are legally responsible.
3. Categories of information we may process

Not every category is collected for every person. The enabled features, selected plan, church settings, administrator choices and information actually supplied determine the records involved. Churches should configure forms and imports to collect only what is necessary for a stated purpose.

Online payment checkout is handled by the applicable payment provider. Our ordinary checkout is not designed to collect or store complete payment-card numbers, card security codes, banking passwords or payment PINs. We may receive transaction references, status, payer or billing details and provider authorisation tokens. Do not enter card credentials into free-text fields, support messages or church records.
4. Where information comes from

A person who supplies someone else’s information must have appropriate authority, provide necessary notices and establish a lawful basis. Knowing someone’s contact details, being a church member or holding an administrator role does not automatically authorise every use of that person’s information.
5. Purposes and legal grounds

We do not treat the fact that processing is useful as a sufficient legal ground. A church must determine the lawful basis for each of its purposes and any additional condition needed for sensitive or children’s data. Contractual necessity does not automatically justify processing the personal information of every member or visitor.

Where we rely on legitimate interests for our own processing, we consider necessity, proportionality and the effect on individuals. Where we rely on consent, withdrawal affects future consent-based processing but does not undo lawful processing already carried out or remove another valid retention obligation.
6. Religious beliefs, pastoral information and other sensitive records

Being identified in a church database can reveal religious beliefs even when a record does not contain a field labelled ‘religion’. Pastoral notes, family circumstances, health information and other records may create additional sensitivity. Churches must assess those risks, collect the minimum necessary, identify a lawful condition for sensitive-data processing and limit access to people with a legitimate need.

A church’s religious or charitable purpose does not create an unrestricted permission to collect, disclose, market with or publish sensitive personal information. Any statutory exception must be evaluated against its actual conditions. In particular, public disclosure or sharing with unrelated organisations requires separate consideration.

The platform includes permission and branch controls, and selected categories of secrets or records receive additional protection. This does not mean all stored information is end-to-end encrypted or inaccessible to every authorised service operator. Administrators must configure permissions carefully and avoid placing highly confidential information in ordinary messages, AI questions, public forms or broadly accessible attachments.

BelivrHQ is not a medical records system, crisis response service, safeguarding authority or substitute for professional counselling. Do not use it to bypass professional confidentiality requirements, mandatory reporting duties or legal restrictions on particularly sensitive information.
7. Children and people requiring additional protection

An individual creating or administering a BelivrHQ account must be at least 18 and legally capable of acting for the relevant organisation. Children may nevertheless appear in church records, such as family, attendance or event records, under the church’s responsibility.

Before entering a child’s information, the church must determine whether parental or guardian authorisation, age or authority verification, an appropriate legal exception, or another safeguard is required. Only information needed for the specified activity should be collected. Photographs, family contact details, health information and public sharing require particular care.

Parents and guardians may contact the responsible church or our designated contact to raise a concern. We may need to verify the requester’s authority and coordinate with the church. We will not disclose a child’s record to an unverified person or assume that every person claiming to be a relative has access rights.
8. Sharing and recipients

We do not sell church member lists or license identifiable church records to advertisers. We do not permit an unrelated church to browse another church’s records simply because both use BelivrHQ. A customer can still expose its own data through an export, public link, misconfigured permission, incorrect recipient or compromised account; the relevant controller remains responsible for those choices, and we remain responsible for our own legal duties.

We seek to limit operational access to what is needed for the relevant function and to use appropriate contractual and security arrangements with providers. A provider acting independently for fraud prevention, payment processing or its own account services may have separate controller responsibilities and its own notice.
9. Technology providers and optional integrations

This table explains providers and provider options reflected in the product; it does not mean every provider receives every record or is enabled for every church. Available integrations and deployed providers can change. Contact us for information relevant to a particular feature, processing arrangement or proposed new service provider.

A church must review its own providers’ terms, privacy notices, locations, charges and permissions before enabling an integration. Disabling an integration can stop future application use but does not necessarily delete data already held by that provider or cancel the church’s separate provider contract.
10. Ask BelivrHQ, analytics and calculated indicators

Ask BelivrHQ is a product guidance feature. Depending on configuration, it can answer from product references or request an AI-generated explanation. When external synthesis is used, the submitted question, recent user-question context, selected references and verified access context are sent to the configured AI provider. The current integration requests that the provider not store the response as a stored API response; that setting is not a promise of zero provider retention for all operational or security purposes.

The assistant is not given general tools to inspect member records, make payments, change permissions or act on your behalf. Nevertheless, text you type can itself contain personal information. Do not submit passwords, payment credentials, pastoral notes, health details or identifiable member information that is unnecessary for a product question.

Enabled reporting or scoring features may calculate attendance patterns, engagement summaries or follow-up indicators from church activity. These are administrative indicators that can be incomplete or wrong. The church must explain its use where required, check the underlying information, provide meaningful human review and avoid treating a score as a determination of a person’s faith, health, entitlement, character or suitability.

We do not intend these features to make legally or similarly significant decisions about people solely by automated means. If you believe a church is using them that way, contact that church and you may also contact us. Applicable rights relating to profiling, objections and human review remain available.
11. Cookies, browser storage and device information

BelivrHQ uses first-party session cookies to support authentication and session continuity. The web application uses HttpOnly cookies for its principal session tokens; persistent session cookies may be set for up to 30 days, while the validity and revocation of the underlying session can differ. Clearing cookies or ending a session can require you to sign in again.

Browser storage may retain interface preferences, selected billing currency, short-lived payment coordination information and cached application resources. Installed web-app resources and previously enabled device features can also leave local data. Signing out is not a guarantee that every downloaded file, browser backup, third-party cookie or previously saved device record has been removed.

The Tawk.to widget can load automatically for eligible active administrators on supported workspace or help pages, and may use its own cookies or storage. Optional embeds and configured monitoring services may also receive connection or device information. We do not claim that all third-party technologies operate without identifiers or that the website currently provides a universal cookie-preferences centre.

You can inspect, block or remove cookies and site storage through your browser, decline to open third-party links or embeds, and contact us about a particular technology. Blocking essential storage can prevent sign-in or other requested functionality. Where a technology requires prior consent or additional controls under applicable law, that requirement applies independently of this notice and commercial acceptance.
12. Service messages and church communications

Account verification, invitations, sign-in security, password recovery, subscription confirmations, renewals and important service notices are operational communications. They are distinct from optional marketing. Some are necessary to provide a requested account or transaction and cannot be disabled while retaining the relevant function.

A church controls its own broadcasts and member communications. It must establish an appropriate permission or consent, identify the sender, honour objections and opt-outs, and comply with the relevant channel’s rules. BelivrHQ does not convert a contact upload into permission to send promotional or sensitive messages.

If an unwanted message relates to a particular church, contact the church or follow its supplied opt-out instructions. Contact us about suspected abuse of the platform. We may need the sender, date, delivery channel and a limited copy of the message to investigate; avoid forwarding unrelated sensitive records.
13. International processing and transfers

Hosting, authentication, storage, monitoring, support, AI and communications providers may process information outside Nigeria. A user or customer may also access the service or export information from another country. Unless expressly agreed in writing, no subscription plan promises that all information stays in Nigeria or in one particular region.

A transfer requiring a legal safeguard must be supported by an applicable transfer basis, such as an appropriate level of protection, recognised contractual or other safeguards, or a specific lawful exception. A church’s choice to use an overseas provider does not remove that requirement. We do not treat acceptance of this Policy as blanket consent to every international transfer.

Contact us for information about the processing arrangements relevant to your use. If a customer needs a particular residency commitment, transfer instrument or additional processing restriction, it must be agreed before that customer relies on the platform for that requirement. Provider locations and contractual safeguards should be assessed for the actual deployment rather than inferred from a provider’s brand name.
14. Security and confidentiality

Our application uses measures intended to protect information, including authentication, permission and church/branch scope checks, session controls, security logging, protection of selected secrets, and encrypted transport where configured for production. Selected integration credentials, authenticator secrets and pastoral content have additional encryption controls. Their existence does not mean every category is end-to-end encrypted, that a security incident is impossible, or that a regulatory certification has been obtained.

The customer must use strong unique passwords, enable appropriate multi-factor authentication, review access and invitations, protect its own devices, limit exports and promptly remove access that is no longer needed. Shared accounts, unmanaged downloads and incorrect public-sharing settings can defeat otherwise appropriate safeguards.

Report suspected unauthorised access promptly through the designated contact. We may verify authority and use a secure channel before exchanging evidence. Do not send active passwords, secret keys, recovery codes or entire member databases in ordinary email. Where a personal-data breach triggers legal duties, we will assess it and provide required notices or assistance without undue delay and within applicable legal time limits.
15. Retention, inactivity and deletion

Information is retained according to the purpose, customer instructions, the status of the relevant account or record, legal requirements, security needs and legitimate claims. A stopped subscription does not itself mean that every underlying church record or payment record is immediately deleted. Deleting a login is different from deleting all business records associated with that person.

Current maintenance routines include removal of inactive member records that have not been updated for more than approximately 365 days and audit logs older than approximately two years when the applicable background jobs run. The inactive-member cleanup can also remove linked records. These are application housekeeping settings, not a statutory retention period or a guarantee that all related copies are deleted on a particular day. Deployment, job operation, record relationships and lawful preservation requirements can affect execution.

Financial, subscription, dispute, legal and security information can require different periods. A valid erasure request, legal hold or specific customer processing agreement may require a different outcome from ordinary housekeeping. We assess the relevant category and legal basis rather than assuming that all information has the same retention period.

Some records are first archived or deactivated and can remain accessible to appropriately authorised users. Permanent deletion may be irreversible. Copies may also exist in exports, recipient inboxes, the customer’s systems, provider records or backups. Where a retained backup contains deleted information, it should remain protected and subject to its applicable recovery and replacement arrangements; restored data may require deletion instructions to be applied again.

We do not publish a universal backup-erasure deadline or promise a fixed post-termination export window that is not supported by the applicable agreement. Customers should export necessary records while access remains available and contact us before closure to agree any assistance, return or deletion arrangements. We will not retain identifiable information indefinitely merely because no fixed period appears in this Policy.
16. Your rights and choices
Subject to the applicable law, our role and legitimate exceptions, you may be entitled to exercise the rights listed below.

Not every request requires release of an entire church database, another person’s information, security secrets or legally privileged material. We may need to redact, separate or preserve information to protect other rights or comply with law. Where we refuse or limit a request, we will explain the reason to the extent legally permitted and identify available review or complaint options.

Your church can often correct ordinary records directly. You do not have to pay for a subscription or use an administrator-only chat channel to raise a privacy request with us. Requests concerning our own controller activities should be sent directly to our designated email.
17. How to make a request

Email lucasdeekay98@gmail.com with the subject “BelivrHQ Privacy Request”. Describe the request, the church involved where relevant, the email or other identifier associated with the record, and a safe reply channel. Provide only the information reasonably needed to locate the record and understand the request.

We may request proportionate proof of identity, authority or guardianship before acting. A rights request is not an instruction to send a password or provide excessive identification. If ordinary email is unsuitable for the evidence involved, ask us to arrange an appropriate channel before sending it.

We will respond without undue delay and within the time required by applicable law. Where a lawful extension, clarification, refusal or referral is necessary, we will explain it as required. Rights requests are ordinarily handled without charge; a fee or refusal will be considered only where the relevant law permits it and with the required explanation.
18. Public links, exports and connected destinations

A public form, publicly available media asset, external link, receipt attachment or export may be accessible outside the ordinary workspace permission controls. Anyone receiving an exported file or forwarded link may retain another copy. A browser download cannot generally be recalled from another person’s device through BelivrHQ.

Customers must check recipient addresses, branch selections, link visibility and the fields included in an export before sharing. People completing a public church form should read the church’s explanation of collection and avoid submitting unnecessary confidential information. The church is responsible for the questions it creates and the lawful use of responses.

Third-party sites and embedded services apply their own practices when you access them. We do not control those practices solely because a link or embed appears in BelivrHQ. This does not remove any responsibility we have for our own selection or use of a provider.
19. Business information, feedback and aggregate information

Business contact information can still be personal information. Feedback, bug reports and support correspondence should not contain unnecessary member records or confidential material. We may use feedback to improve the product, but a feedback licence does not give us an unrestricted right to disclose personal information or republish a church’s confidential records.

We may use genuinely anonymised or appropriately aggregated information for reliability, planning and product analysis. Information that can reasonably be linked back to a person remains subject to applicable privacy requirements; merely removing a name or using an identifier does not necessarily make it anonymous.
We do not use identifiable church records as an advertising audience or claim an unrestricted licence to train general-purpose AI models on the contents of customer workspaces.
20. Questions and regulatory complaints

Contact PappyCoder Technologies Limited at lucasdeekay98@gmail.com to raise a concern about our processing. For a church-controlled record, identify the church so that we can involve the responsible administrator where appropriate. You may complain about BelivrHQ directly when the concern relates to our own conduct.

You may also complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission through its official channels at ndpc.gov.ng, or to another competent regulator where applicable. Contacting us first can help resolve a concern, but this Policy does not impose a contractual barrier to a regulatory complaint, an urgent application or another mandatory remedy.
21. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy to reflect changes to the service, our processing or applicable requirements. The version and date shown on this page identify the current published text. For material changes, we will provide additional notice where required or appropriate, such as an administrator email or a prominent service notice.

A revised notice does not retroactively make an incompatible use lawful or replace consent where fresh consent is required. We will identify an appropriate basis before implementing a new use that requires one. Keep a copy of the version relevant to your engagement if you need a historical record.
22. Company and privacy contact
Operator: PappyCoder Technologies Limited. Country: Nigeria. Product: BelivrHQ. Designated privacy and legal contact: lucasdeekay98@gmail.com.

This mailbox is designated by the company for BelivrHQ privacy, legal and contractual notices even though the address is not on a company-branded domain. A published contact change will not invalidate a request already properly sent to the previous address. Ask for the appropriate postal or formal service details if your matter requires physical delivery or a procedure prescribed by law.
Contact PappyCoder Technologies Limited
For BelivrHQ privacy requests, legal notices or contractual enquiries, email lucasdeekay98@gmail.com. You do not need a BelivrHQ account to use this contact.
Describe the matter and provide a safe reply channel. Do not send passwords, recovery codes, provider keys or unnecessary sensitive church records.

A provider acting independently for fraud prevention, payment processing or its own account services may have separate controller responsibilities and its own notice.
9. Technology providers and optional integrations

This table explains providers and provider options reflected in the product; it does not mean every provider receives every record or is enabled for every church. Available integrations and deployed providers can change. Contact us for information relevant to a particular feature, processing arrangement or proposed new service provider.

A church must review its own providers’ terms, privacy notices, locations, charges and permissions before enabling an integration. Disabling an integration can stop future application use but does not necessarily delete data already held by that provider or cancel the church’s separate provider contract.
10. Ask BelivrHQ, analytics and calculated indicators

Ask BelivrHQ is a product guidance feature. Depending on configuration, it can answer from product references or request an AI-generated explanation. When external synthesis is used, the submitted question, recent user-question context, selected references and verified access context are sent to the configured AI provider. The current integration requests that the provider not store the response as a stored API response; that setting is not a promise of zero provider retention for all operational or security purposes.

The assistant is not given general tools to inspect member records, make payments, change permissions or act on your behalf. Nevertheless, text you type can itself contain personal information. Do not submit passwords, payment credentials, pastoral notes, health details or identifiable member information that is unnecessary for a product question.

Enabled reporting or scoring features may calculate attendance patterns, engagement summaries or follow-up indicators from church activity. These are administrative indicators that can be incomplete or wrong. The church must explain its use where required, check the underlying information, provide meaningful human review and avoid treating a score as a determination of a person’s faith, health, entitlement, character or suitability.

We do not intend these features to make legally or similarly significant decisions about people solely by automated means. If you believe a church is using them that way, contact that church and you may also contact us. Applicable rights relating to profiling, objections and human review remain available.
11. Cookies, browser storage and device information

BelivrHQ uses first-party session cookies to support authentication and session continuity. The web application uses HttpOnly cookies for its principal session tokens; persistent session cookies may be set for up to 30 days, while the validity and revocation of the underlying session can differ. Clearing cookies or ending a session can require you to sign in again.

Browser storage may retain interface preferences, selected billing currency, short-lived payment coordination information and cached application resources. Installed web-app resources and previously enabled device features can also leave local data. Signing out is not a guarantee that every downloaded file, browser backup, third-party cookie or previously saved device record has been removed.

The Tawk.to widget can load automatically for eligible active administrators on supported workspace or help pages, and may use its own cookies or storage. Optional embeds and configured monitoring services may also receive connection or device information. We do not claim that all third-party technologies operate without identifiers or that the website currently provides a universal cookie-preferences centre.

You can inspect, block or remove cookies and site storage through your browser, decline to open third-party links or embeds, and contact us about a particular technology. Blocking essential storage can prevent sign-in or other requested functionality. Where a technology requires prior consent or additional controls under applicable law, that requirement applies independently of this notice and commercial acceptance.
12. Service messages and church communications

Account verification, invitations, sign-in security, password recovery, subscription confirmations, renewals and important service notices are operational communications. They are distinct from optional marketing. Some are necessary to provide a requested account or transaction and cannot be disabled while retaining the relevant function.

A church controls its own broadcasts and member communications. It must establish an appropriate permission or consent, identify the sender, honour objections and opt-outs, and comply with the relevant channel’s rules. BelivrHQ does not convert a contact upload into permission to send promotional or sensitive messages.

If an unwanted message relates to a particular church, contact the church or follow its supplied opt-out instructions. Contact us about suspected abuse of the platform. We may need the sender, date, delivery channel and a limited copy of the message to investigate; avoid forwarding unrelated sensitive records.
13. International processing and transfers

Hosting, authentication, storage, monitoring, support, AI and communications providers may process information outside Nigeria. A user or customer may also access the service or export information from another country. Unless expressly agreed in writing, no subscription plan promises that all information stays in Nigeria or in one particular region.

A transfer requiring a legal safeguard must be supported by an applicable transfer basis, such as an appropriate level of protection, recognised contractual or other safeguards, or a specific lawful exception. A church’s choice to use an overseas provider does not remove that requirement. We do not treat acceptance of this Policy as blanket consent to every international transfer.

Contact us for information about the processing arrangements relevant to your use. If a customer needs a particular residency commitment, transfer instrument or additional processing restriction, it must be agreed before that customer relies on the platform for that requirement. Provider locations and contractual safeguards should be assessed for the actual deployment rather than inferred from a provider’s brand name.
14. Security and confidentiality

Our application uses measures intended to protect information, including authentication, permission and church/branch scope checks, session controls, security logging, protection of selected secrets, and encrypted transport where configured for production. Selected integration credentials, authenticator secrets and pastoral content have additional encryption controls. Their existence does not mean every category is end-to-end encrypted, that a security incident is impossible, or that a regulatory certification has been obtained.

The customer must use strong unique passwords, enable appropriate multi-factor authentication, review access and invitations, protect its own devices, limit exports and promptly remove access that is no longer needed. Shared accounts, unmanaged downloads and incorrect public-sharing settings can defeat otherwise appropriate safeguards.

Report suspected unauthorised access promptly through the designated contact. We may verify authority and use a secure channel before exchanging evidence. Do not send active passwords, secret keys, recovery codes or entire member databases in ordinary email. Where a personal-data breach triggers legal duties, we will assess it and provide required notices or assistance without undue delay and within applicable legal time limits.
15. Retention, inactivity and deletion

Information is retained according to the purpose, customer instructions, the status of the relevant account or record, legal requirements, security needs and legitimate claims. A stopped subscription does not itself mean that every underlying church record or payment record is immediately deleted. Deleting a login is different from deleting all business records associated with that person.

Current maintenance routines include removal of inactive member records that have not been updated for more than approximately 365 days and audit logs older than approximately two years when the applicable background jobs run. The inactive-member cleanup can also remove linked records. These are application housekeeping settings, not a statutory retention period or a guarantee that all related copies are deleted on a particular day. Deployment, job operation, record relationships and lawful preservation requirements can affect execution.

Financial, subscription, dispute, legal and security information can require different periods. A valid erasure request, legal hold or specific customer processing agreement may require a different outcome from ordinary housekeeping. We assess the relevant category and legal basis rather than assuming that all information has the same retention period.

Some records are first archived or deactivated and can remain accessible to appropriately authorised users. Permanent deletion may be irreversible. Copies may also exist in exports, recipient inboxes, the customer’s systems, provider records or backups. Where a retained backup contains deleted information, it should remain protected and subject to its applicable recovery and replacement arrangements; restored data may require deletion instructions to be applied again.

We do not publish a universal backup-erasure deadline or promise a fixed post-termination export window that is not supported by the applicable agreement. Customers should export necessary records while access remains available and contact us before closure to agree any assistance, return or deletion arrangements. We will not retain identifiable information indefinitely merely because no fixed period appears in this Policy.
16. Your rights and choices
Subject to the applicable law, our role and legitimate exceptions, you may be entitled to exercise the rights listed below.

Not every request requires release of an entire church database, another person’s information, security secrets or legally privileged material. We may need to redact, separate or preserve information to protect other rights or comply with law. Where we refuse or limit a request, we will explain the reason to the extent legally permitted and identify available review or complaint options.

Your church can often correct ordinary records directly. You do not have to pay for a subscription or use an administrator-only chat channel to raise a privacy request with us. Requests concerning our own controller activities should be sent directly to our designated email.
17. How to make a request

Email lucasdeekay98@gmail.com with the subject “BelivrHQ Privacy Request”. Describe the request, the church involved where relevant, the email or other identifier associated with the record, and a safe reply channel. Provide only the information reasonably needed to locate the record and understand the request.

We may request proportionate proof of identity, authority or guardianship before acting. A rights request is not an instruction to send a password or provide excessive identification. If ordinary email is unsuitable for the evidence involved, ask us to arrange an appropriate channel before sending it.

We will respond without undue delay and within the time required by applicable law. Where a lawful extension, clarification, refusal or referral is necessary, we will explain it as required. Rights requests are ordinarily handled without charge; a fee or refusal will be considered only where the relevant law permits it and with the required explanation.
18. Public links, exports and connected destinations

A public form, publicly available media asset, external link, receipt attachment or export may be accessible outside the ordinary workspace permission controls. Anyone receiving an exported file or forwarded link may retain another copy. A browser download cannot generally be recalled from another person’s device through BelivrHQ.

Customers must check recipient addresses, branch selections, link visibility and the fields included in an export before sharing. People completing a public church form should read the church’s explanation of collection and avoid submitting unnecessary confidential information. The church is responsible for the questions it creates and the lawful use of responses.

Third-party sites and embedded services apply their own practices when you access them. We do not control those practices solely because a link or embed appears in BelivrHQ. This does not remove any responsibility we have for our own selection or use of a provider.
19. Business information, feedback and aggregate information

Business contact information can still be personal information. Feedback, bug reports and support correspondence should not contain unnecessary member records or confidential material. We may use feedback to improve the product, but a feedback licence does not give us an unrestricted right to disclose personal information or republish a church’s confidential records.

We may use genuinely anonymised or appropriately aggregated information for reliability, planning and product analysis. Information that can reasonably be linked back to a person remains subject to applicable privacy requirements; merely removing a name or using an identifier does not necessarily make it anonymous.
We do not use identifiable church records as an advertising audience or claim an unrestricted licence to train general-purpose AI models on the contents of customer workspaces.
20. Questions and regulatory complaints

Contact PappyCoder Technologies Limited at lucasdeekay98@gmail.com to raise a concern about our processing. For a church-controlled record, identify the church so that we can involve the responsible administrator where appropriate. You may complain about BelivrHQ directly when the concern relates to our own conduct.

You may also complain to the Nigeria Data Protection Commission through its official channels at ndpc.gov.ng, or to another competent regulator where applicable. Contacting us first can help resolve a concern, but this Policy does not impose a contractual barrier to a regulatory complaint, an urgent application or another mandatory remedy.
21. Changes to this Policy

We may update this Policy to reflect changes to the service, our processing or applicable requirements. The version and date shown on this page identify the current published text. For material changes, we will provide additional notice where required or appropriate, such as an administrator email or a prominent service notice.

A revised notice does not retroactively make an incompatible use lawful or replace consent where fresh consent is required. We will identify an appropriate basis before implementing a new use that requires one. Keep a copy of the version relevant to your engagement if you need a historical record.
22. Company and privacy contact
Operator: PappyCoder Technologies Limited. Country: Nigeria. Product: BelivrHQ. Designated privacy and legal contact: lucasdeekay98@gmail.com.

This mailbox is designated by the company for BelivrHQ privacy, legal and contractual notices even though the address is not on a company-branded domain. A published contact change will not invalidate a request already properly sent to the previous address. Ask for the appropriate postal or formal service details if your matter requires physical delivery or a procedure prescribed by law.
Contact PappyCoder Technologies Limited
For BelivrHQ privacy requests, legal notices or contractual enquiries, email lucasdeekay98@gmail.com. You do not need a BelivrHQ account to use this contact.
Describe the matter and provide a safe reply channel. Do not send passwords, recovery codes, provider keys or unnecessary sensitive church records.

The subscription agreement governing BelivrHQ accounts, customer responsibilities, payment, data processing, service availability and allocation of risk.
PappyCoder Technologies Limited · Nigeria
On this page

These Terms of Service ("Terms") govern access to the BelivrHQ hosted platform and related account, support and subscription services supplied by PappyCoder Technologies Limited, Nigeria ("Company", "BelivrHQ", "we", "us" or "our"). "Customer" or "you" means the church, ministry or other organisation subscribing to the service; an individual user must also comply with obligations applicable to that user.

An authorised representative accepts these Terms when expressly agreeing during registration or another acceptance process. A person acting for an organisation represents that they have authority to bind it. If you do not have that authority, do not create or purchase a workspace on its behalf. Access by invited users is subject to the customer’s valid agreement and each user’s applicable obligations.

These Terms include provisions on payment, customer responsibility, suspension, customer indemnity, warranty qualifications and limits of liability. Those provisions allocate commercial risk and should be read before acceptance or payment. They do not exclude any right, duty or remedy that cannot lawfully be excluded.
Important points to read first
These points help you navigate the document. Read the full provisions that follow.
1. Definitions and contract structure

‘Service’ means the BelivrHQ hosted software and related functions made available under the selected plan. ‘Workspace’ means the customer’s church environment, including its branches and authorised users. ‘Customer Data’ means records, files, messages, form responses, personal information and other material submitted to or generated for the customer through the Service. ‘Authorised User’ means a person the customer validly permits to access its workspace. ‘Order’ means a checkout, accepted quotation or separately signed order identifying the service, plan, term, price or additional scope.

The Order identifies commercial selections; these Terms supply the general service conditions. Our Website Terms and Conditions govern public website use and supplement the acceptable-use rules. Our Privacy Policy explains personal-information practices. It is not an unrestricted licence to process personal information or a substitute for a required controller–processor agreement.

If documents conflict, mandatory law prevails. A separately signed agreement or processing addendum controls the subject it expressly addresses. An Order overrides these Terms only for its expressly stated commercial scope or identified exceptions. The data-processing provisions in section 16 control processor activities; these Terms otherwise control the Service over general Website Terms. The Privacy Policy does not reduce statutory privacy rights.
2. Eligibility, authority and permitted customers

An account holder must be at least 18, legally capable of contracting and authorised for the access they request. Information supplied at registration must be accurate and kept reasonably current. You must not impersonate a church, administrator, provider, donor or another person, register using an identity you do not control, or misrepresent authority over an organisation.

The Service is offered for lawful church, ministry and related organisational administration. You must determine whether your intended activity is lawful and suitable in each relevant location. Access is not permitted where prohibited by applicable sanctions, export controls or another binding restriction. We may reasonably request information needed to verify an account, resolve competing ownership claims or satisfy legal obligations.

A person acting only as an employee or volunteer does not automatically become personally responsible for the customer’s subscription debt solely by being invited. That person remains responsible for their own unlawful acts, misuse of credentials and obligations expressly applicable to individual users.
3. Access licence and reserved rights

Subject to the Order, payment where required and compliance with these Terms, we grant the customer a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable right during the authorised service period to let its Authorised Users access the Service for the customer’s internal lawful activities. This is access to hosted functionality, not a sale of the platform, source code, infrastructure, underlying models or intellectual property.

You may not resell, sublicense, lease or commercially provide shared access to unrelated organisations without our written agreement. A multi-branch plan permits the locations and organisational scope allowed by that plan; it does not permit an undisclosed hosting or resale business. Technical access to an endpoint does not expand the licence or override permissions, quotas or plan restrictions.

Rights not expressly granted remain with their owner. We may use technical controls to protect subscription entitlements, tenant boundaries, service integrity and authorised access, subject to applicable law and the commitments in these Terms.
4. Accounts, administrators and access security

The customer appoints its administrators and remains responsible for inviting suitable users, selecting branches, assigning roles, reviewing permissions and removing access promptly when employment, volunteering or other authority ends. HQ access permits broader organisational scope where the product allows it; it is not a substitute for individual permissions or a right to access another customer’s workspace.

Use individual accounts, strong unique credentials and appropriate multi-factor authentication. Keep recovery codes and provider keys confidential, protect devices and email accounts, and notify us promptly of suspected compromise. Do not share credentials to evade staff limits, allow an unauthorised person to use a session, or test another customer’s access boundaries.

Actions performed through a valid account may be treated as authorised for ordinary service administration unless we know or reasonably ought to know otherwise. This allocation does not make the customer responsible for an incident caused by our own failure to meet a non-excludable duty. We may require verification or temporarily restrict access where a credible compromise, ownership dispute or unauthorised instruction is suspected.
5. Plans, limits and feature entitlements

The selected plan governs available features, member or staff capacity, locations, roles, storage or other limits shown in the applicable Order and product billing information. Permissions and the customer’s settings can further restrict a feature. Buying a plan does not automatically grant every user access to all features included in it.

Current Essentials, Community and Network offerings have different staff, location and role capabilities; custom roles are restricted to eligible higher plans. Enterprise scope must be agreed. The plan description presented at purchase and any express Order terms control the purchased scope, rather than an assumption based on another customer’s configuration or an old screenshot.

If you downgrade or a subscription expires, additions, particular roles, exports or other paid functionality may be restricted. Existing records are not a guarantee of continued editing, creation or access under a lower entitlement. You must review limits and make necessary arrangements before a downgrade or expiry. We will not treat an entitlement reduction as permission to disclose customer records to another organisation.
6. Fees, billing periods, quotes and currency

You agree to pay the amount, currency and billing period you authorise in the Order. Standard plans may be offered monthly or annually; an annual payment purchases the stated annual period rather than twelve separately cancellable monthly instalments unless the Order says otherwise. Enterprise fees, implementation work or additional services require a separate agreement where not included in the displayed offer.

Displayed conversions or starting prices are informational until confirmed by an applicable quote or checkout. The checkout may use a supported charge currency different from a display currency. Review the exact amount and currency before paying. Your bank or provider may impose conversion, processing, cross-border or other fees under its own agreement; BelivrHQ does not set those third-party charges merely by displaying a converted estimate.

A quote can expire. A pending checkout may preserve the amount and currency recorded when it was created, even if a later display or quote changes. Review any resumed payment before authorisation. Do not create duplicate payments because a return page is delayed; use the available verification process or contact us with the payment reference.

Fees exclude taxes only where clearly stated. Applicable taxes, withholdings and any required supporting documents will be treated according to law and the Order. We do not impose a tax gross-up or hidden surcharge merely through a general clause in these Terms. We may correct an obvious pricing error before accepting a new Order, provide the corrected information and let you decline it; we will not silently substitute a higher amount after payment approval.
7. Payment authorisation, activation and verification

The payer must be authorised to use the selected payment method. Payment processing is performed by the provider identified at checkout. Access activation depends on verified payment and successful application to the relevant church subscription, not only a browser redirect, screenshot, debit alert or unverified client message.

A pending, failed, disputed, reversed, duplicated or mismatched transaction may need reconciliation. We may request a reference and limited evidence needed to investigate. Never send a banking password, payment PIN, card security code or full secret payment credentials to support. A provider’s fraud screening or settlement delay is not a promise that we have received cleared payment.

If payment is received but cannot be applied correctly, we will investigate and provide an appropriate correction or refund where due. We may suspend unpaid or fraudulently obtained access while a genuine payment issue is resolved, subject to mandatory rights and reasonable handling of evidence. We will not intentionally charge twice for the same verified service period.
8. Manual renewals, upgrades and downgrades

Standard BelivrHQ subscription renewals are currently manual. Selecting a plan, entering a payment method at a one-off checkout or receiving a reminder does not itself authorise recurring platform subscription debits. A future automatic-renewal arrangement would require appropriate disclosure and payment authorisation before it applies.

The customer must renew in time to avoid interruption. Reminder delivery is not guaranteed, and a missed reminder does not by itself extend a paid period. The dates and status shown by the verified subscription record determine the applicable period, subject to correction of errors and any express Order terms.

An eligible mid-period upgrade may use the prorated calculation shown in the quote and retain the existing renewal date. A downgrade may be scheduled for the next renewal and does not necessarily create an immediate refund or credit. The confirmed quote and resulting subscription record control the specific change; the interface’s displayed action must be reviewed before confirmation.

Recurring giving is different from platform subscription renewal. A donor’s authorisation to a church and that church’s payment provider may permit recurring donations according to the donor’s separate mandate, even while the church’s BelivrHQ software subscription renews manually.
9. Cancellation, refunds and billing disputes

You may stop renewing the standard subscription. To request earlier account closure, assistance with cancellation or a refund review, contact our designated email and identify the church and relevant payment. Do not assume there is a self-service cancellation, refund or complete database-deletion button where the product does not provide one.

Except where the Order or mandatory law provides otherwise, a voluntary decision to stop using an otherwise properly supplied paid service does not automatically entitle you to a refund for the unused portion. This qualification does not exclude remedies for defective or misdescribed services, duplicate or unauthorised charges, a failure to deliver an agreed service, or any statutory cancellation or refund right.

We will assess genuine billing complaints and provide the remedy required by the circumstances and law, which may include correction, re-performance, a reasonable partial refund or another appropriate outcome. If we permanently discontinue a prepaid service for our convenience and do not provide a reasonably equivalent agreed alternative, we will refund the unused prepaid portion attributable to the discontinued service, subject to any more favourable mandatory right.

Raise a suspected billing error promptly with the reference, date, amount, currency and reason for dispute. A request for prompt notice is not a contractual waiver of a statutory claim period. A chargeback is not a substitute for an unsupported allegation, and you must not knowingly initiate a fraudulent dispute; equally, these Terms do not prohibit a genuine payment dispute or a lawful remedy through your bank, provider, regulator or court.

Provider reversal and settlement times vary. We cannot promise an exact bank posting date or recover fees retained by an independent provider unless our agreement or law requires it. Approved refunds will ordinarily follow the original payment route or another verified lawful arrangement.
10. Future price and product changes

We may change prices, plan packaging or functionality for future Orders or renewal periods. We will make material commercial changes clear before you authorise the affected payment. A general right to update the product is not permission to charge a higher amount during an already paid fixed term without an agreed basis.

We may make maintenance, security, legal and product improvements during a term. If a change materially removes an expressly purchased core function during an unexpired paid period, we will consider an appropriate alternative or remedy rather than relying only on a broad variation clause. Roadmaps, illustrative previews, beta screens and informal discussions are not binding delivery commitments unless expressly included in the Order.
11. Customer responsibilities and record accuracy

You are responsible for the lawfulness, accuracy, relevance and permitted use of Customer Data and instructions supplied by your organisation. Obtain necessary notices, consents, licences and authority before uploading personal information, photographs, sermons, copyrighted material, financial details or confidential records. Maintain appropriate procedures for member corrections, data-subject requests, safeguarding and staff changes.

Check dates, currencies, branch assignments, donor or member selections, account names, recipient destinations, import mappings and generated reports before relying on them. A receipt records information associated with the relevant transaction; it is not automatically a bank confirmation, a tax-deductibility certificate, an independent audit or proof that a provider has settled funds.

You must maintain appropriate reconciliation, accounting, audit and record-preservation processes. Review exports, retain necessary independent copies and arrange continuity for critical church operations. These responsibilities do not relieve us of our own agreed service duties or legal obligations.

The customer must supply an operational contact and ensure important notices can reach an authorised decision-maker. A dispute between church officers, branches, denominations, employees or volunteers does not authorise us to transfer control without reasonable evidence or to act as an arbiter of religious governance.
12. Acceptable use and prohibited conduct

We may investigate credible misuse, preserve proportionate evidence and take the measures described in section 21. We do not undertake to pre-screen every record or message or to act as the customer’s compliance officer. The Website Terms contain additional public-site use rules.
13. Giving, ticketing and payment-provider relationships

BelivrHQ supplies software for recording giving, producing receipts, managing events or tickets and connecting supported payment services. Unless a separate written agreement expressly says otherwise, we are not the receiving church, fundraiser, donation beneficiary, event organiser, bank, insurer, custodian, escrow service, payment institution or financial adviser.

The relevant church is responsible for its merchant/provider account, bank details, beneficiary information, authority to collect funds, event delivery, donor communications, cancellations and applicable tax treatment. Payment providers control their own onboarding, authorisations, fraud screening, processing, chargebacks, settlement and provider fees. An integration or generated receipt is not an endorsement of a church’s activities or a guarantee of settlement or refund.

A donor or ticket holder’s dispute about the underlying donation, event, recurring mandate or church promise should ordinarily be raised with the receiving church and relevant provider. We can assist with platform records where authorised or legally required. This allocation does not excuse a platform error or unlawful act for which we are responsible.

Manual cash or bank records depend on information entered by authorised users and may not be independently verified by a connected provider. A customer must not issue a misleading receipt, imply tax relief we have not verified, or represent a recorded amount as settled money without checking the appropriate evidence.
14. Communications, integrations and external providers

Church-selected email, SMS, WhatsApp, calling, payment and webhook services generally require the customer’s own compatible provider accounts, enabled settings and appropriate credentials. Provider charges, recipient restrictions, sender approvals, message-template rules and service availability are separate from the BelivrHQ subscription unless an Order expressly includes them.

You authorise processing and transmission reasonably necessary for the integrations you enable and remain responsible for the legality of those instructions. Keep provider accounts funded where required and credentials current. Platform account emails may use our organisation’s providers even when a church’s own broadcast integration is disabled.

Queueing, API acceptance or a ‘sent’ processing status does not guarantee inbox placement, device delivery, call completion, WhatsApp approval, payment settlement or a recipient’s response. External services can filter, delay, reject, change or discontinue functionality. We will handle our own integration duties with reasonable care but do not control an independent provider’s entire service.

Disabling or removing an integration does not necessarily undo completed deliveries, recall information, cancel a provider contract or revoke a donor mandate. You must take any additional steps required with that provider. We may disable a connection that is insecure, unlawful, incompatible or credibly abusive, subject to proportionate handling and applicable rights.
15. Customer Data, intellectual property and confidentiality

As between the parties, the customer and its licensors retain their rights in Customer Data. You grant us only the rights reasonably needed to host, copy, transmit, process, display, secure, maintain and support that data for the Service, the agreed instructions and our lawful obligations. This licence does not transfer ownership of member information or permit an unrelated advertising use of identifiable church records.
